DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph 10 February 2021 ATTY. MARK A. MADALANG, JR. Madalang Law Office Suite 314, Laperal Bldg., Session Road Baguio City Dear Atty. Madalang: This has reference to your letter dated 1 July 2020, seeking this Department's opinion concerning the refusal of the Office of the Governor to sign duly accomplished vouchers of a Sangguniang Panlalawigan member and its deliberate delay in the release of the same. As represented in your letter, a client of yours, who is a Sangguniang Panlalawigan member (hereto referred as X) "was allocated a budget for the last 4 quarters for the year 2020 being an integral part of the Annual Provincial Budget of Province Y. " However, despite the budget duly allocated to X's office, the Office of the Provincial Administrator and ultimately the Office of the Governor thereat deliberately delayed the release or refused to sign the duly accomplished vouchers of X, despite several follow-ups made by the latter. Under such premise, arose your request for a legal opinion on the following issues, which we quote in toto: 1. Legal consequences and/or propriety of the actions of the Executive Office? 2. Legal consequences and/or propriety of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan refusing to allocate any budget at the office of Provincial Board Member X against his consent and knowledge in the Provincial budget of 2021? Foremost, attention is directed to the pertinent provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160), thus:

"Section 336. Use of Appropriated Funds and Savings.- Funds shall be available exclusively for the specific purpose for which they have been appropriated. No ordinance shall be passed authorizing any transfer of appropriations from one item to another. However, the local chief executive or the presiding officer of the sanggunian concerned may, by ordinance, be authorized to augment any item in the approved annual budget for their respective offices from savings in other items within the same expense class of their respective appropriations." Accordingly, when the funds are already within the coffers of the LGU for its appropriation and disposition, it behooves upon the local chief executive or the vice-governor to comply with the procedural requirements in the disposition thereof. Otherwise, the local chief executive or the vice- governor may be held liable for dereliction/neglect of duty pursuant to the Local Government Code. For this purpose, an administrative case may be filed before the Office of the President, which is the proper forum to resolve the matter. It should be emphasized, however, that neither the Provincial Administrator nor the Office of the Governor has the authority and power to sign disbursement vouchers. Section 466 of the Local Government Code is categorical when it provides, viz: "Section 466. Powers, Duties, and Compensation. (a) The vice-governor shall: Be the presiding officer of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and sign all warrants drawn on the provincial treasury for all the expenditures appropriated for the operation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan" (emphasized supplied) Based on the aforequoted provision, it is the Vice-Governor who has the power and authority to sign all warrants drawn on the provincial treasury for all expenditures appropriated for the operation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan such as disbursement vouchers. Corollarily, Section 344 of the same Code provides, viz: Section 344. Certification, and Approval of, Vouchers. - No money shall be disbursed unless the local budget officer certifies to the

existence of appropriation that has been legally made for the purpose, the local accountant has obligated said appropriation, and the local treasurer certifies to the availability of funds for the purpose. Vouchers and payrolls shall be certified to and approved by the head of the department or office who has administrative control of the fund concerned, as to validity, propriety, and legality of the claim involved. Except in cases of disbursements involving regularly recurring administrative expenses such as payrolls for regular or permanent employees, expenses for light, water, telephone and telegraph services, remittances to government creditor agencies such as GSIS, SSS, LDP, DBP, National Printing Office, Procurement Service of the DBM and others, approval of the disbursement voucher by the local chief executive himself shall be required whenever local funds are disbursed. In cases of special or trust funds, disbursements shall be approved by the administrator of the fund. In case of temporary absence or incapacity of the department head or chief of office, the officer next-in-rank shall automatically perform his function and he shall be fully responsible therefor. Anent the second issue, the refusal of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to allocate any budget for the office of X, if unjustified, may result to a liability for dereliction/neglect of duty. An action for mandamus before a court of law pursuant to the Rules of Court is proper. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. oc- LLLS/27 Copy furnished: DIR. MARLO L. IRINGAN Regional Director, DILG-CAR Barangay Center, Upper Session Road Baguio City Very truly yours, the Authority of the Secretary: L INGAN , CESO Ill Undersecretary for Local Government
